isolated_kernel_timing_a100d.box: a100d (this agent, contended throughout) and a100b (the lead, confirmed exclusive: nvidia-smi 0% util, 296 MiB) — both boxes' kernel-only numbers agree to within 0.3%, so the artifact cites both; the exclusive a100b run is the number of record. This section went through TWO fix rounds.
isolated_kernel_timing_a100d.round_1_method_fixed_but_incomplete: Per-ITERATION Device::synchronize() (never one sync batching N launches), >=20 warm-ups, >=200 timed iterations, min AND median (fixed fold order, f64::total_cmp) — see tests/cuda_parity.rs's time_kernel(). This closed the ORIGINAL batching defect (0.7459 ms REFUTED — a re-run of that flawed method spread 2.35x across repeats, 0.273/0.619/0.641/0.321 ms) but was NOT sufficient: the lead's own exclusive-box re-run of round 1's committed harness (a100b, 0% util, 296 MiB) still measured cast_scale_bf16_f32 at ~2.12 ms (5.24% roofline), not the ~0.21 ms/53% this agent had attributed to a clean re-measurement. That attribution was WRONG — see round_2 below.
isolated_kernel_timing_a100d.round_2_root_cause_and_fix: The lead found the actual cause: apply1 allocates its 151 MB f32 OUTPUT storage INSIDE launch on EVERY iteration (device.alloc::<f32>(n), src/cuda/cast_scale.rs), and cudarc has NO caching allocator — a fresh cuMemAlloc, freed via Drop at the end of every timed iteration, is genuinely ~2 ms of device-driver work, not a measurement artifact, and NOT the pod contention this agent had (incorrectly) blamed round 1's own contended re-measurement attempts on. cast_add_bf16's 25 MB output pays far less of this tax, which is why ITS number was already accurate in round 1. FIX: cast_scale_bf16_f32_into/cast_add_bf16_into (#[doc(hidden)] pub, ops/cast_scale.rs) launch the IDENTICAL kernel into a Tensor allocated ONCE outside the timed loop, backed by pub(crate) cuda_launch_*_into functions in src/cuda/cast_scale.rs that reuse the exact launch config/module/kernel name as the production path. tests/cuda_parity.rs now measures and prints BOTH numbers, labelled: 'wrapper' (apply1/apply2, what a real caller pays, alloc included) and 'kernel-only' (preallocated output). A correctness assertion (bit-identical vs apply1/apply2, flattened) runs before either timing loop, so a bug in the new path could not silently make the kernel-only number meaningless.
